scope: Proposition H.1 (Transfer of a fixed scalar score) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 164-165. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the uniform constrained-sampler inputs of Proposition G.1. Fix ϵ > 0 and prescribe pre bounds for the input complexities and for ρ−1, τ−1, where ρ, τ > 0. Include these data in the prescribed finite collection of sampler requests and choose the later parameters in the order of Section H.4. Fix a tuple of centers and sample ψ : T → U by the normalized law (F.4). Suppose f : U → [0, 1], λ ∈ [0, 1], and a fixed positive patch formula T∗(u, β) of the prescribed complexity with d∗ additional slots satisfy Pr ψ ( there exists an allowed slice B ⊆ T such that Et∈B(f(ψ(t)) − λ)T∗(ψ(t), β(ψ(t))) ≥ ρ ) ≥ τ. The inner average is uniform on B, which may be chosen separately for each path; the probability uses the fixed-center law without conditioning on this event. Then there is an ambient slice and a positive patch with at most d∗ + X h dim Wh 164 slots having positive score against f − (1 − ϵ)λ. The output complexity and the logarithm of the reciprocal score may additionally use the allowed late parameters and the heights of bases of the Wh: both have polynomial bounds in the resulting augmented logarithmic budget, as does the cost of the output slice.
